details.comment1: Chiller is not a real redump but a "fixed" ROM. While the PRG could be read correctly the CHR differed from each cart according to bootgod. A little investigation from my side reveiled that the CHR appears to be intended to match the HES-version (HES CHR could easily be confirmed by extracting from the Maxi 15 pack). There was also an [!] US-version in GoodNES V3.23b matching this CHR (but slightly different PRG?) so I went and merged the good PRG with the good CHR.

Only MD5 hash and title screen images were released. ROM was restored to match this MD5 checksum. Each 128KB part of the ROM also matches the written checksum-16 on the ROM chip stickers.
The difference is at 0x416. Hacked data: 00 00 00 41 50 52 49 4C 00 12 10 10 19 00 00 4E 41 00 56 45 52 53 49 4F 4E 00 00 17 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 0A 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00

details.comment1: Software from e-Reader cards is stored in a proprietary vpk compression format within the save file. Trimming the save file down to just the vpk file and decompressing it using nvpktool gets you the ROM.

As a form of copy protection, NES-e series ROMs have bytes 0x3FFA, 0x3FFB, and sometimes 0x3FFD changed so that the ROM is unusable in emulators and flashcarts. These bytes are changed back to what they're supposed to be by the e-Reader's NES emulator by the time the ROM is loaded into memory.

details.comment1: Software from e-Reader cards is stored in a proprietary vpk compression format within the save file. Trimming the save file down to just the vpk file and decompressing it using nvpktool gets you the ROM.

As what may be a form of copy protection, NES-e series ROMs have bytes 0x3FFA, 0x3FFB, and sometimes 0x3FFD changed so that the ROM is unusable in emulators and flashcarts. These bytes are changed back to what they're supposed to be by the e-Reader's NES emulator by the time the ROM is loaded into memory.

details.comment1:
Demo Vision ROM dump --------------------
Dumped 3/16/2006 by Chris C.
The Demo Vision is an oldskool GameBoy development kit consisting of a large unit in a steel case, and 1 or 2 GameBoy units that connect to it via cables. The GameBoys are wired to draw power from the main unit, and to send their audio and video data to the main unit. Games are inserted directly into the GameBoys, and the image and sound are displayed simultaneously on the GB screen & speaker and Demo Vision's A/V outputs.
Inside the Demo Vision are up to 2 NES/Famicom motherboards, each with individual RF and composite AV outputs. Each NES has EPROMs for PRG and CHR data, and there is an on-board MMC5 mapper (to control timing/RAM??). The CHR ROM is revision A, and the PRG ROM is revision B.
The EPROM data are identical to the "Demo Boy" dumped by Mark Knibbs, so the only real difference is that this dump has the mapper set correctly, and thus has correct colours and graphics when run on an emulator. Enjoy!

details.comment1: Files were extracted using Unity Assets Bundle Extractor 2.1c using the sharedassets0.assets file from each respective version of the game. The asset for each ROM image was named "game". When extracted, the switch file was close to 384kb and the PC version was 736kb. archive.name: Millipede
archive.sticky_note:
Some info on the game based on the links in the source:
Early build of never finished game for Famicom. This is Namco version which has nothing to do with the final Famicom version from Atari.
This project was by Atari for Namcot in Japan for the Famicom specifically, this was never a planned U.S. title, it's an unreleased Famicom game. Documentation in the repo shows that they halted development when they realized they didn't actually have the full rights to the game. There was some discussion about re-theming the game to a space themed Millipede clone, but that probably never went anywhere.

details.comment1: As what may be a form of copy protection, NES-e series ROMs have bytes 0x3FFA, 0x3FFB, and sometimes 0x3FFD changed so that the ROM is unusable in emulators and flashcarts. These bytes are changed back to what they're supposed to be by the e-Reader's NES emulator by the time the ROM is loaded into memory.

details.tool: Analogue Nt Mini (v1) + Jailbreak 2.0 (CopyNES with BATMAPS.bin plugin)
details.comment2:
Uploaded by re4mat to archive.org Comment from archive.org item: ``` This is the NES 2.0 ROM of Super Russian Roulette, dumped over the summer in a group effort. It required creating a custom plugin (BATMAPS.BIN, included) for CopyNES, as the game itself uses a custom mapper (on a CPLD) to access the over 8MB of digital speech. It was dumped using CopyNES on an Analogue Nt Mini (v1) with the Jailbreak 2.0 firmware and the aforementioned BATMAPS plugin.
Currently, the mapper has only been implemented in a version of Nintendulator (included), making that the only way so far to play it aside from a real cartridge. To get the ROM to play on hardware devices or other emulators, they will each need to implement the custom mapper used by the game.
(Update: 31 December, 2020) The latest jailbreak firmware for the Nt Mini Noir added the Super Russian Roulette mapper (#413), so the ROM should now be playable on that system.
(Update: 29 January, 2021) Mapper 413 is now supported on MiSTer. ```

details.comment1: The board appears to use all standard parts, except for the GB CPU. The things with stickers on them are the BIOS ROM, and two PAL chips. I guess those are programmable logic chips which control the graphics decoding and/or mapping into the VRAM (chip) of the Famicom. The board has no company markings on it, except for the stickers, which have an "Intelligent Systems co.ltd." name and logo on them. The name of the board is "DMG DEB (B)", suggesting that this is the second revision of the WideBoy.

details.comment1: Some normally invalid opcodes were repurposed as a form of copy protection to prevent ROMS extracted from the collection from working in other emulators. Supporting this behavior in the NES 2.0 standard would require defining a new console type entry. However, due to how few ROMs support this behavior and this behavior not being present in any hardware, no console type entry is planned to be defined for this behavior. As such, the header used here is the incorrect one that is found when extracting the ROMs from the collection.

details.comment1: Some normally invalid opcodes were repurposed as a form of copy protection to prevent ROMS extracted from the collection from working in other emulators. Supporting this behavior in the NES 2.0 standard would require defining a new console type entry. However, due to how few ROMs support this behavior and this behavior not being present in any hardware, no console type entry is planned to be defined for this behavior. As such, the header used here is the incorrect one that is found when extracting the ROMs from the collection.

archive.name: Titenic
archive.datter_note: multicart extract from New Year 15-in-1

details.comment1:
From NRS: "The common ROM file of the Hummer Team game Titenic is actually an extract from the Super New Year Cart 15-in-1 multicart that had its cutscenes and title screen restored by Санчес. It is not the actual version of the game that was released by ABAB Soft.
The proper version of the game, released by ABAB Soft, does not have the music that would later be heard in Harry's Legend. Instead, it has Hummer Cheng arrangements of the James Horner film score, including the (in)famous Celine Dion song. It also prominently displays the game's name in the status bar at all times."
Not verified according to GoodNES V3.23b

This is the original Bit Corp. release of Othello, which is more commonly known in its release from Australia's Home Entertainment Suppliers (HES), which we consider to be "rev1". Why? Because the original Bit Corp. version (rev0) does not run on standard NES/Famicom consoles as well as most Famiclones! Othello (rev0) uses the 6502 CPU's "decimal" mode to display the number of pieces you have on the playfield. Nintendo's 6502 clone, the Ricoh RP2A03, however has the decimal mode functionality removed for cost reasons, and almost all Famiclones replicate that removal. Bit Corp.'s famiclone, the "Creator", keeps the decimal mode, and Othello (along with the rev0 version of Duck Maze, commonly referred as Duck) relies on it.

archive.name: 240p Test Suite with Gus's Game Collection
archive.sticky_note: Digital version released pre-compiled as a ROM along with the source code. The "special thanks to Backer" section of the credits was already blanked out with 10 in hex in the ROM as distributed. This is located at a slightly different offset than it is in the physical version, which does not match this ROM otherwise either. It was originally launched as a Kickstarter physical, and the source code retains that screen, although the final ROM is different. Appears to be v0.23 of the 240p Test Suite, though has Zapper navigation unlike any other so far.

details.project: Video Game History Foundation, The Cutting Room Floor
details.comment2:
[Link 4: https://www.videogamesage.com/forums/topic/16379-punch-out-black-box-nes-prototype-found]
Release consisted of video of joint effort by the Video Game History Foundation (video) and The Cutting Room Floor (TCRF) admin Xkeeper (TCRF page with ROM upload). Cartridge owner stated as being anonymous, in the video and TCRF page.
Unusually retail-like PCB and ROM chips.
Photos are cropped from the video, except the PCB back photo, which is from the VideoGameSage thread
Video attached, but in low quality to save space
Posts by GameHistoryOrg (gamehistoryorg / 282661653080834048) (Frank Cifaldi's discord account) post on Hidden Palace discord: "Punch-Out was submitted to WATA by Heritage. I believe the poster on VGS is from Heritage. It was an NOA garage sale find. I just looked at it on Wednesday, but I'm not going to post the report etc until they do since I don't think it would be right to do that before the person who actually paid for it gets it" "It is pretty early though. No audio, only four boxers, very simple behavior. I talked to them about it and don't think there is any chance for the ROM being public outside of someone winning the eventual Heritage auction." (links: https://discord.com/channels/615298215905853442/1045238561173159967/1469705182584504362 https://discord.com/channels/615298215905853442/1045238561173159967/1469706519162392647)
PSA certification is linked on the Heritage Auctions page: https://www.psavideogames.com/cert/details/
